review:
Frederic: Resurrection of Music Director’s Cut, developed and published by Forever Entertainment S. A., is a rhythm game that builds its entire identity around personality, humor, and an unusual reverence for classical music. The premise alone is enough to set it apart: Frédéric Chopin is brought back to life in a modern world where music has lost its soul, and he must reclaim it through a series of over-the-top musical duels. It’s a deliberately absurd setup, but one that gives the game a strong narrative backbone and a clear sense of direction, something not all rhythm titles attempt.

The gameplay revolves around a note-matching system that borrows familiar ideas from arcade rhythm games but adapts them into a piano-inspired format. Instead of relying on the typical colored lanes seen in genre staples, the game uses a seven-key layout that loosely mirrors musical notes, giving it a more “instrumental” feel. Notes scroll toward the player in time with the music, and precision is key to maintaining combos and building momentum. Each track functions as a battle, where performance directly affects the outcome, turning songs into competitive encounters rather than simple score challenges. This adds a layer of tension that keeps even shorter tracks engaging.

What truly carries the experience, however, is the soundtrack. Rather than leaning on modern or licensed music, the game reinterprets Chopin’s compositions across a wide range of styles. Classical pieces are transformed into energetic rock arrangements, electronic remixes, and other genre-bending variations that keep the music feeling fresh and unpredictable. These reinterpretations are often creative and playful, giving the game a unique identity within the rhythm genre. Even players who may not typically gravitate toward classical music can find themselves drawn in by how accessible and lively these versions feel.

The presentation leans heavily into a cartoonish, almost satirical tone. Story segments are delivered through comic-style cutscenes filled with exaggerated characters and humor that borders on absurdity. Chopin’s opponents are intentionally larger-than-life, often embodying exaggerated cultural or musical stereotypes. While this approach gives the game a distinctive charm, it can also be hit-or-miss depending on the player’s tolerance for its style of humor. Some will find it amusing and memorable, while others may see it as overly chaotic or inconsistent in tone.

Mechanically, the game shows both creativity and roughness. The seven-key system, while interesting, is not always intuitive, especially for newcomers who are more familiar with standard rhythm layouts. Visual clarity can occasionally suffer, making it harder to track incoming notes during more complex sections. As the difficulty increases, these issues become more noticeable, and the experience can shift from satisfying to slightly frustrating. There’s a sense that the core idea is strong, but the execution lacks the level of polish seen in more refined rhythm titles.

Content-wise, the game offers a relatively brief campaign that can be completed in a few hours. While there is some replay value in chasing higher scores and tackling harder difficulties, the overall package feels somewhat limited once all tracks have been experienced. The lack of additional modes or expanded progression systems means that the game relies heavily on its charm and music to sustain interest, which may not be enough for players seeking a longer-lasting experience.

Despite its shortcomings, Frederic: Resurrection of Music Director’s Cut succeeds in carving out its own niche. It’s a game that prioritizes creativity and personality over technical perfection, and that approach gives it a memorable quality that many more polished titles lack. There’s a clear sense of passion behind its design, particularly in how it celebrates and reimagines Chopin’s work in a modern, playful context.

In the end, this is a rhythm game that thrives on its uniqueness. It doesn’t always deliver the smoothest or most refined gameplay, but it offers something genuinely different, wrapped in a package full of humor and musical experimentation. For players willing to embrace its quirks, it can be an entertaining and distinctive experience, even if it doesn’t reach the heights of the genre’s best.

Frederic: Resurrection of Music — это музыкальный платформер в стиле ретро, разработанный студией Forever Entertainment. Игра выпущена в 2017 году и является ремейком оригинальной игры Frederic: The Musicais с улучшенной графикой, звуком и новыми режимами. Це́тельски стилизованная под 8-битную эпоху, она сочетает элементы платформера, музыкальной ритм-игры и приключения, предлагая уникальный опыт для любителей ретро.

Основные особенности
1. Геймплей и механика
Платформер с музыкальной тематикой:
Игрок управляет Фредериком — музыкантом-карабиниром, путешествующим по миру, чтобы восстановить свою музыку. Главное здесь — сочетание классического платформинга и музыкальных элементов.

Музыкальные ритмы:
Во время боёв и действий нужно синхронизироваться с музыкой, нажимая клавиши в ритме мелодий, что расширяет игровой процесс и добавляет уникальности.

Уровни и секреты:
Игра насыщена разнообразными уровнями, где нужно избегать препятствий, сражаться с врагами и искать скрытые секреты.

Улучшения и боссы:
В игре есть босс-файты и возможности улучшать навыки героя, делая его более сильным и адаптирующимся к сложностям.

2. Графика и стиль
Ретро-стиль в духе 8-битных платформеров с яркими, простыми пиксельными графиками.
Красочные анимации и выразительный дизайн персонажей создают атмосферу светлого и ностальгического ретро.
3. Музыка и звук
Главная особенность игры — качественный чиптюновый саундтрек, вдохновлённый классическими 8-битными мелодиями.
Музыкальные композиции прекрасно сочетаются с геймплеем, создавая синергию между ритмом и действиями игрока.
Почему стоит играть
Уникальное сочетание платформера и ритм-игры:
Интересное и необычное сочетание элементов, требующее реакции и чувства ритма.

Ностальгия и стиль:
Игра отлично передает атмосферу классических ретро-игр, что порадует поклонников старой школы.

Качество музыкального сопровождения:
Восхитительные мелодии создают запоминающийся игровой опыт.

Разнообразие уровней и режимов:
В игре много секретов, боссов и испытаний, что увеличивает её реиграбельность.

Минусы:
Может показаться сложной для новичков из-за необходимости ловко нажимать клавиши под музыку.
Ограниченная графика — характерная для ретро-стиля, что не каждому по вкусу.

For the price, I'd absolutely recommend this to anyone who enjoys rhythm games or anyone who enjoys games with such a fun concept as this. But I'd be hard-pressed to defend a lot of the core aspects of the game.

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Frederic: Resurrection of Music Director's Cut, Forever Entertainment tarafından geliştirilen ve yayınlanan bir müzik oyunudur. Oyuncular, Frédéric Chopin'in ruhunu yeniden canlandırmaya çalışan bir rock yıldızı olan Frederic'in kontrolünü ele alıyor.

Oyunda, Frederic'in müzikle dolu bir maceraya atılması gerekiyor. Oyuncular, ritim tabanlı bulmacaları tamamlamak için çeşitli hareketleri yapmak zorundadır. Her müzik parçası için farklı hareketler gerekir ve oyuncular doğru hamleleri yaparak müziğin ritmine uygun hareket ederler. Oyuncuların başarısı, yıldızları kazanmalarını sağlar ve bu da yeni bölümlerin kilidini açar.

Oyunun müzikleri, Chopin'in klasik eserlerinin modern bir yorumuyla yapılmıştır ve oyunda rock, pop, elektronik ve diğer müzik tarzlarından etkilenmiştir. Bu nedenle, oyuncular hem klasik müzik hem de modern müzik sevenler için keyifli bir deneyim yaşayabilirler.

Görsel açıdan, oyunun grafikleri ve animasyonları oldukça renkli ve canlıdır. Karakterlerin animasyonları ve müzikle uyumlu hareketleri, oyuncuların müziğin ritmine ve atmosferine daha iyi dalmasına yardımcı olur.

Frederic: Resurrection of Music Director's Cut, müzik sevenler için benzersiz bir oyun deneyimi sunar. Zorlu ritim tabanlı bulmacaları, benzersiz müzikleri ve renkli grafikleri ile oyunculara keyifli bir müzik yolculuğu sunar.

I love this game. I keep coming back to it, because it has great gameplay. STEEP learning curve: the game expects you to master nine keyboard keys AND remember the rhythm of each song. But once you get it, the game is great fun. Solid cutscene animation and funny characters keeps the gameplay from getting dry. Works really well on ubuntu linux desktop versions. Also, be aware that there is a "Directors Version" on steam, sold separately, which seems to have additional features. I think it has some additional levels and multiplayer, but reviews say that the gameplay may not be as responsive. I decided on getting this version, and I would recommend others to do the same.

After many hours practicing, I beat the game on expert level, and I am now working on the Chopin (highest) level. There are a few games that I have beaten at all on steam, and Frederic is the only one that I played again at a harder difficulty. So, you see that this is one of my most favorite games.

I never played the Rock Band games, so I never thought that I was interested in rhythm games. For some reason, I gave Frederic enough time to understand the game play. Frederic does a faaaaantastic job easing the player into more difficult levels. I struggled with this game at first, but each day I saw myself get better. Not just learning the notes, but also being quicker and more accurate. Not only that, Frederic gives you a deep appreciation of the music, by crafting the keys through the spirit of the song. When I am in the flow, getting the keys of a difficult song with barely a thought, I feel like I am right there jamming with Frederic. It is a moving experience.

This game uses the Unity Game Engine. It takes 1,700 MBs of diskspace. I played this game with the keyboard only, with an ubuntu linux desktop with radeon mesa graphic drivers, but it needed a Steam Launch Option fix to start.

I recommend this game to anyone who can appreciate music, and it will show them a deeper appreciation for music, tonality, and rhythm. The Frederic games are some of my favorite Steam games, and I keep coming back to them again and again. I am very grateful for the experiences. The games are often on sale for less than a dollar, and the purchase comes with the soundtrack.

This game is going to require an investment of your time. It is a challenging game, even at the easiest levels. You want a great rhythm game for a great price? You will have a great time learning the Frederic's songs. Also, your purchase price also gets you all the game songs as MP3 local files. This is easily the best "price for enjoyment" game that I have in my steam llibrary!

Frederic: Resurrection of Music Director's Cut es un juego que le brinda un homenaje bastante curioso al legado de Frédéric Chopin quien es considerado uno de los mayores representantes del romanticismo musical. Básicamente el juego tiene las mismas mecánicas del Guitar Hero pero no con guitarra sino con un piano; 

El juego presenta una historia bastante alocada y está narrada como si de un cómic se tratase, las cosas se ponen interesantes tras la resurrección de Chopin a manos de unas musas quienes le encargan una honrosa misión para hacerle frente al flagelo de la música moderna. Chopin deberá de enfrentar a varios géneros y estilos musicales, que van desde el hip-hop, tecno, música indú, reggae,  e inclusive música de anime (un otaku te reta a muerte tras hacer una broma respecto a su waifu), la historia es bastante divertida con un interesante giro de los acontecimientos al final. La jugabilidad creo que pudo mejorar bastante, puesto que los controles son difíciles de dominar por ende perderás bastante tiempo hasta encontrar la configuración apropiada para tu estilo de juego. Otro detalle que me disgustó fue que el actor que le da la voz a Chopin no le pone ganas ni hace 
 énfasis en algunas situaciones importantes, parece que solo se puso a leer el guión cuando andaba estreñido y así lo dejaron.

El juego posee un modo multijugador que está bastante muerto, tardé como 3 meses en encontrar a alguien dispuesto a jugarlo conmigo. 
Dejando de lado los problemas que pueda llegar a tener, vale la pena sobretodo si lo compras cuando tenga descuento porque llega a estar casi regalado, es un juego que te hará salir de la rutina puesto que es bastante desafiante en los niveles más altos, y es muy reconfortante cuando logras superar a algún rival tras varios intentos fallidos, es más te llegas a sentir como un verdadero pianista.
